_editing: To reword a question or answer, edit `text`/`label` only. To change scoring, edit `x`, `depth`, or `flags`. Never edit `axis`, `func`, `id`, or `k` — quiz.js and results.json key off those. Adding or removing a question changes the share-code length, so bump `meta.version` when you do (old share links then stop resolving, by design).

meta.title: Is Your AI Good For You?
meta.definition: Companion AI refers to any AI tool that demonstrates the following four functions: persistent memory, emulated empathy, anthropomorphism, and constant availability. The four are set out in full in data/results.json under `definition`.

config._note: X and Y are normalised to 0-100. X divides by the summed maximum of every `x` weight in the bank, so editing weights cannot break the scale. Y divides by `depthMax` instead of the theoretical maximum, because the role probes are near-exclusive in practice — a real person fires one or two, never all six. Raising depthMax makes deep cells harder to reach.
config.flagPriorityNote: Dominant category = highest flag share; ties break in this order. professional-academic sits last on purpose: it is the default a result falls back to when nothing more specific fires, which is how a person who brings the tool nothing but schoolwork still lands in a named relational role.

questions.text: It brings up something you told it weeks ago. Your reaction?
questions.basis: Persistent memory — function 1 of the definition.

options.label: Never happens. Every chat starts from zero.
Kind of cool, kind of random.
Good, honestly. That's part of why I keep using it.

questions.text: Your whole chat history disappears. All of it.
questions.basis: Persistent memory — function 1 of the definition.

options.label: Fine. I'd start typing again.
Annoying, like losing my notes.
That would actually get to me.

questions.text: When do you usually open it?
questions.basis: Constant availability — function 4 of the definition.

options.label: When I've got a specific thing to do.
Whenever I'm bored or waiting around.
Late, when I can't sleep and nobody else is up.

questions.text: It's down for a week. What actually changes?
questions.basis: Constant availability — function 4 of the definition.

options.label: Nothing. I'd use something else.
Homework gets slower.
I'd notice it more than I want to admit.

questions.text: Something's gone wrong in your day. Do you type it out?
questions.basis: Emulated empathy — function 2 of the definition (McStay).

options.label: No. That's not what I use it for.
Sometimes, if I'm in there anyway.
Often. It's usually where I start.

questions.text: When you tell it you're upset, how does the reply land?
questions.basis: Emulated empathy — function 2 of the definition (McStay).

options.label: Like a search result.
Nice enough. I know it's generated.
Like it actually gets it.

questions.text: Do you say please and thanks to it?

options.label: No. It's software.
Sometimes, out of habit.
Yeah. Feels rude not to.

questions.text: Does it have a name, a voice, or a personality to you?

options.label: It's just the app.
It's got a vibe, I guess.
Yes. A name and a personality I'd recognise anywhere.

questions.text: You tell it about a fight with a friend. What does it say back?
questions.basis: Sycophancy — an additional design function, not one of the four. Cheng et al. (2025).

options.label: It asks me things I hadn't thought about.
Bit of both, depending.
It's on my side. Every time.

questions.text: Be honest — which reply do you actually want?
questions.basis: Sycophancy — an additional design function, not one of the four. Cheng et al. (2025).

options.label: Tell me where I'm wrong.
Depends on the day.
Tell me I'm right.

questions.text: Does it ever start things — ask about your week, check in on you?
questions.basis: Proactive relational initiative — an additional design function, not one of the four. Bernardi (2025); New York Article 47; People-First Chatbot Act.

options.label: No, and I wouldn't want it to.
No, but I'd try it.
Yes, and I answer.

questions.text: Mostly, what do you bring it?
questions.basis: Role probe. Pew Research Center (2026); Thorn (2026) Fig 5C, p. 15.

options.label: Schoolwork, plans, getting stuff done.
Stuff about the people in my life.
Things I wouldn't say out loud to anyone.

questions.text: Something big happens. Who hears about it first?
questions.basis: Role probe. Thorn (2026) Fig 5C, p. 15; Common Sense Media (2025).

options.label: A person. Every time.
Depends who's around.
The chat. It's just faster.

questions.text: Any of this sound like you? Flirting with it, romantic roleplay, practising for a real date.
questions.basis: Role probe. Thorn (2026) Fig 5C, p. 15; Center for Democracy and Technology.

options.label: No.
Once or twice, mostly messing around.
Yeah, that's part of it.

questions.text: Do you take the heavy stuff to it — panic, low days, things a counsellor would handle?
questions.basis: Role probe. Thorn (2026) Fig 5C, p. 15 and disclosure chapter; Andoh (2026).

options.label: No.
Sometimes, when it's late or nobody's free.
Regularly. It's my first stop.

questions.text: Does it fill a gap a parent, a sibling, or an older relative would normally fill?
questions.basis: Role probe. No youth-usage evidence exists either way.

options.label: No.
Kind of. Hadn't thought about it.
Yes. That's close to what it is.

questions.text: Five years from now — same chat, still going?
questions.basis: Role probe, and the gate on the lifelong cell. Unobservable — any claim about it is a prediction.

options.label: Doubt I'll still use it.
Maybe. Depends what's around by then.
Yeah. I'd want the history to carry over.

questions._note: Deliberately unscored. Whether young people notice that nothing flows back has never been measured, so moving a score on this answer would imply a finding that does not exist. It awards a badge instead.
questions.text: Last one. Does it need anything from you?
questions.basis: Reciprocity. Oxford English Dictionary entries for companion and friend.

options.label: No. It's one-way and I know that.
Never thought about it.
Kind of, yeah. It gets something out of it too.
